sources.title: DeepSeek API Change Log
sources.evidence: The alias already received an upgrade on 2024-05-17; 2025-12-01 is its V3.2 upgrade. The April 2026 entry maps it to V4-Flash non-thinking. Later V4.1 compatibility mappings name different aliases.

sources.title: DeepSeek V4 Preview Release
sources.evidence: April 24, 2026 announcement explicitly maps deepseek-chat to V4-Flash non-thinking, gives Flash 284B total and 13B active parameters, and makes 1M context standard. Announces legacy alias inaccessibility after July 24, 2026 at 15:59 UTC.

sources.title: DeepSeek-V4-Flash model card
sources.evidence: Exact preview Flash card identifies released text-generation weights, 284B total/13B activated, 1M context, and MIT licensing of repository and weights. Its non-thinking evaluation includes tool-agent benchmarks. The separate Hugging Face storage-size badge says 291B, not the developer nominal model count.

sources.title: DeepSeek-V4: Towards Highly Efficient Million-Token Context Intelligence
sources.evidence: Sections 2 and 4.2.1 specify Transformer architecture with MoE feed-forward layers and hybrid compressed attention. Exact Flash configuration has 43 Transformer layers, 284B total parameters and 13B activated per token.

sources.title: DeepSeek API Upgrade: Chat Prefix Completion, FIM, Function Calling and JSON Output
sources.evidence: July 25, 2024 announcement explicitly includes deepseek-chat in the models receiving function calling and text-completion features.

sources.title: DeepSeek Models & Pricing
sources.evidence: Current page lists deepseek-flash and deepseek-v4-pro; compatibility footnote names deepseek-v4-flash and deepseek-v4-flash-vision-exp, but not deepseek-chat. It does not establish this legacy alias still operates.

sources.title: Models.dev deepseek-chat record
sources.evidence: Catalog lead mixes a December 2025 date and V3.2 weight link with 1M context. Primary documentation resolves the later alias mapping; this source is not technical verification.

sources.title: DeepSeek-V3.2 model card
sources.evidence: The baseline weight link opens a V3.2 text-generation model card. It describes the earlier backing model, not the April 2026 alias mapping.

sources.title: Original DeepSeek API update chronology revisited
sources.evidence: Fresh full chronology retrieved. Earliest listed exact deepseek-chat event remains May 17, 2024 and explicitly calls it an upgrade, not first launch. Later V3/V3.2/V4 mapping changes cannot serve as initial release.

sources.title: Immutable May 6, 2024 DeepSeek-V2 launch README
sources.evidence: Original GitHub history identifies commit e23eeb51 at May 6, 2024 14:50Z. Immutable README advertises the native OpenAI-compatible API platform, but does not name the deepseek-chat alias or state that it is the platform's first launch.

sources.title: Original DeepSeek news archive inventory
sources.evidence: Fresh original sitemap and linked news page checked. Available archived product entries start with July 2024 API upgrades; no January 2024 platform launch source was present.

sources.title: Original DeepSeek-LLM repository README checked
sources.evidence: Original full README retrieved. Describes the initial 7B/67B weights and research; no dated initial deepseek-chat API alias launch resolves the catalog target.

name.note: Readable normalization of the official deepseek-chat identifier; a mutable API alias.

developer.note: Developer identified by its own API announcement.

family.note: Broad family retained because the alias has spanned several DeepSeek generations.

release_date.note: Still unresolved: original API changelog starts with an existing-alias upgrade on May 17, 2024. A newly found January 30, 2024 platform-launch lead appears in later Chinese retrospectives, but no original dated announcement tying that launch to the exact deepseek-chat identifier was recovered. The immutable May 6 native README verifies API availability, not initial alias release.

open_weights.note: The last explicitly mapped V4-Flash preview has downloadable weights. This describes its backing checkpoint, not a separate alias checkpoint.

license.note: License of the documented backing weights; hosted-service terms are separate.

parameters_b.note: Developer nominal total in billions for the explicitly mapped preview. No storage-element counting or unproven later alias mapping is used.

active_parameters_b.note: Developer nominal activated parameters per token in billions for that same Flash preview.

architecture.note: Transformer with MoE FFNs, compressed sparse/heavily compressed attention and manifold-constrained hyper-connections; specific to the last documented backing model.

context_window.note: One million tokens for the documented April 2026 mapping; current endpoint availability is not established.

modalities.note: Text chat/completion interface and text-generation backing weights. Later vision aliases are different identifiers.

reasoning.note: Alias selects non-thinking mode; this flag does not mean the backing model cannot solve reasoning tasks.

tool_call.note: Explicit alias function-calling support and later Flash non-thinking tool-agent results establish historical capability, not present service operation.

description.value: Legacy DeepSeek chat API alias, last explicitly mapped to DeepSeek-V4-Flash preview in non-thinking mode; announced for retirement in July 2026.
description.note: Replaces generic capability copy with identity and lifecycle context.

patch.description: Legacy DeepSeek chat API alias, last explicitly mapped to DeepSeek-V4-Flash preview in non-thinking mode; announced for retirement in July 2026.
patch.notes: Specifications describe the explicit April 24, 2026 V4-Flash preview mapping. The original alias launch remains unverified; the former December 1, 2025 date describes its V3.2 upgrade. DeepSeek announced inaccessibility after July 24, 2026, 15:59 UTC; no authenticated endpoint test was performed. Counts are developer nominal model parameters, not Hugging Face storage totals. MIT/open weights refer to the backing checkpoint. Release-date re-audit checked the original news archive and immutable May 6, 2024 V2 README. A January 30, 2024 API-platform launch appears in secondary retrospectives, but its original exact-alias launch evidence remains unverified.

sources.label: V4 preview and legacy alias mapping
Last documented backing weights: V4-Flash preview
Original DeepSeek API update chronology revisited

summary: All 14 fields reviewed. Add primary-supported nominal 284B total/13B active and MoE architecture for the last explicit V4-Flash preview mapping, plus MIT weight license. Clear the upgrade date incorrectly presented as first release. Retain historically documented 1M/text/non-thinking/tool capabilities with retirement and mapping caveats. Original release date and current endpoint operation remain unresolved. Fresh release-date review inspected the native news archive and immutable V2 launch README. It found a January 30, 2024 platform-launch lead in secondary histories but could not verify the original announcement or exact alias mapping; the date remains null.

searches: DeepSeek 开放平台 上线 2023 2024 API
Native sitemap/news, API chronology, DeepSeek-LLM README/issues, immutable DeepSeek-V2 May 6 README
findings: The current official chronology explicitly labels its first exact-alias entry an upgrade.
An immutable May 6 README verifies API availability earlier than the current changelog but does not establish when the alias first launched.

Chinese retrospective https://hub.baai.ac.cn/view/43089 and derivative reports claim January 30, 2024 platform launch with Chat/Coder; this is a lead, not primary proof, and was not promoted into the catalog.
limitations: No primary January 2024 announcement or archived original documentation identifying the rolling alias was recovered.
The original LLM checkpoint, web-chat launch, API-platform launch and later backing-model replacements are distinct events.
